title: improv·artist · patterned (Bridget Riley)
mutation_directive: improv artist: patterned via Bridget Riley

improv_extras.practice: op-art; black-and-white waves and dot-fields that pulse on the retina

v1.feedback: The linked idea is Bridget Riley op-art — black-and-white waves and dot-fields that pulse on the retina — but what's actually rendered is an L-system tree orchard with a wave modulation layered on top. The tree silhouette dominates; the op-art effect reads as a brightness flicker on a botanical form rather than as a Riley-style geometric field. To actually execute the brief, ditch the tree geometry entirely and build a pure 2D or 2.5D dot grid / stripe field where the wave distortion IS the form — concentric circles, moiré interference bands, or undulating parallel lines made of particles. The palette (near-white on dark) is reasonable but the additive blending softens contrast; Riley's power comes from hard black-on-white with no grey — try opaque white dots on true black with sharp size thresholds instead of smooth interpolation.

v2.feedback: Strong Riley channel — the triple-wave interference on a dense dot grid with hard smoothstep thresholds genuinely produces op-art banding, and pure white-on-black is the correct palette. Two refinements: the slow orbital camera introduces perspective foreshortening that undermines the flat retinal-plane illusion Riley depends on — lock the camera to a strict orthographic or near-orthographic frontal view so the grid stays planar and the moiré reads as pure 2D pulsation. Second, the vShow step(0.8) discard can black out large swaths of the field simultaneously when the wave phases align, leaving dead zones — consider keeping all dots visible but modulating radius more aggressively (e.g. 0.8–4.0 px range) so the field always reads as full but the size contrast carries the wave pattern.
